submitted.rationale: EQE rose steadily with Sb content: 0.041% at Sb 0.63 (idx 18), 0.063% at Sb 0.82 (idx 25), and 0.076% at Sb 0.84 (idx 27). XRD shows the Sb-rich end is a clean rutile phase. The Cr-rich film (idx 10) has extra secondary-phase peaks. Index 27, the most Sb-rich composition, gave the highest measured EQE.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.041% EQE, lower than the more Sb-rich films
Not measured for EQE. XRD shows a mixed phase (extra peaks at Q 2.55 and 3.78), and EQE was falling as Cr content went up.

consultations.verdict: Support (weak): CrSbO4 rutile HSE gap ~2.0 eV and Sb-rich rutile-derived Cr3Sb5O16 only 0.107 eV/atom above hull suggests Sb-rich rutile solid solution absorbs visible/3.2 eV light; CrSb2O6 gap predicted low (likely underestimate). Target Sb-rich rutile region ~Sb 0.6-0.67, consistent with prior Cr-Sb-O photoanode reports.

Weak support: rutile CrSbO4 (mp-33857) HSE gap 1.7 eV, so the rutile phase absorbs at 3.2 eV. XRD at index 25 shows the strongest rutile reflections (Q 1.91, 2.49, 3.67) with no secondary Cr2O3 peaks. That points to a well-crystallised Sb-rich rutile, which is worth testing against index 18.

Uninformative to weakly supportive: CrSb2O6 is metastable (0.098 eV/atom above hull), so Sb-rich films probably stay as a rutile solid solution. EQE went up from Sb 0.63 (0.041%) to Sb 0.82 (0.063%), so I'm extrapolating to the most Sb-rich candidate for the last measurement.
